classification.difficultyReason: Graph inequalities using endpoint inclusion and ray direction.

content.prompt: Graph these intervals on the real number line.

answer.short: Closed endpoint at $-1$; ray to the left.
answer.worked: Include $-1$ with a closed circle and draw the interval extending left.

solutionDiagrams.code:
% mathsmap-diagram-colours {"version":1,"kind":"graph","base":[],"semantic":[],"reference":"Exercise 2A 4a, teacher PDF page 5"}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.52cm,y=0.6cm]\special{dvisvgm:raw <metadata data-graph-strokes="1"/>}\draw[->,line width=0.5pt] (-5,0)--(5.2,0) node[right] {$x$};\foreach \x in {-4,...,4}{\draw[line width=0.4pt] (\x,-.08)--(\x,.08);\node[below] at (\x,-.1){\special{dvisvgm:raw <g data-graph-text="tick">}$\x$\special{dvisvgm:raw </g>}};}\draw[<-,line width=0.8pt] (-5,.65)--(-1,.65);\fill (-1,.65) circle (2pt);\end{tikzpicture}

spec.description: Number line with a raised interval ray; the template cannot express interval segments or rays.

answer.short: Open endpoint at $-2$; ray to the right.
answer.worked: Exclude $-2$ with an open circle and draw the interval extending right.

answer.short: Open endpoint at $-3$, closed endpoint at $4$; join them.
answer.worked: Exclude $-3$ with an open circle, include $4$ with a closed circle, and join the endpoints.
